column1: # The engine manifest. One row a file: which engine item it serves, where it is, and what it does.
# item is the thing in the engine plan or the engine table the file exists for. A file that serves no item is a
# file nobody asked for, and a file that is the only one under an item is an item with no second reading.
# kind says what the file is for the loop:
#   derived    written by the compiler from what a target answered. Never authored.
#   seed       partial information given to the compiler. Legitimate, and completed by derivation.
#   key        an answer key. A derivation is checked against it and may never read it.
#   engine     the compiler itself. Knows no target and no vendor.
#   entry      an entry point. Runs the engine against something.
#   scaffold   holds the work up while it is built, and comes out when it is done.

column4: what it does

A tree over the alphabet applied to words, so a tree states what a target must answer.
How much of a relation the ladder's own cases decide. 507 arrangements fit them and are not it.
18 precepts and 9 rewrites, typed. What a derived alphabet is checked against.
12 of the schema's 99 words as trees, typed. What a derived web is checked against.
A tree as one number, so two trees compare without a walk.

3068 arrangements over the 7 anchors. Every cost reads - until the part times one.

Every form a ruleset writes, assembled. 63 forms, 0 refused.
Builds a machine by widening and sweeping, asking a disassembler for names.
36 questions put in the part's own code, each with the answer a person worked out.
A cubin written from text, with one the toolchain built standing as the pattern.
